summary: Ryuichi Abe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Keio, Johns Hopkins, Taisho, and Columbia, he held appointments at Columbia University (1991, 1998–2004) and Harvard University (~2003).

Ryuji Hayashi is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Delhi. His career includes posts at Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, Kodomo Education Hosen University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Ryujo Yamada was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He served as a professor at Tohoku University and held a leadership post at Musashino University.

Ryuken Nawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who has served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Ryuken Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies and was professor emeritus at Taisho University.
Ryuo was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at Tō-ji and Koyasan University.
Ryusei Keira is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Lausanne under the supervision of Tom Tillemans.
Ryushin Kitao is a scholar of Buddhist studies who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University.
Takanobu Saitō is a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with the Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism, Bukkyo University, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.

Ryushin Sudo was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Taisho University. He served as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryushin Uryuzu was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He was affiliated with the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute and served as a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1978–1997).

Ryusho Hikata specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Junjirō Takakusu at the University of Tokyo and earning a doctorate from Tohoku University. He taught at Kyushu University, served as president of Fukuoka Women's University, and joined the Japan Academy.
Ryuta Kikutani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who has held positions at Tohoku University, Kyoto University, and Koyasan University.

Ryutaro Tsuchida is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and completed doctoral work under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg. He held posts at Marburg (~1978–1983) and the University of Tokyo (1983, 1995–2012).

Takayoku Kimura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1980), a lecturer at Yamaguchi University, and head priest at Kaichō-ji.
Ryuyu Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kenyo Mitomo and founded the Nikaya Buddhism Thought Research Association.
Ryuzan Nishimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa.
Ryōmin Akizuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950) and held a post at Saitama Medical University (~1972–1991).
Rüdiger Schmitt is an Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and linguistics scholar. He studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1963–1965) and served at Saarland University (~1972–2004).
S. D. Laddu is an Indologist and linguist who held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University and served as editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
